reasons: Directionality is correct: under this Site Development and Hosting Agreement HDI is the provider (designs, develops, hosts the Site and supplies software/technology) and the Company is our client, so an HDI-to-Company indemnity runs in our favour.

The 'missing' status is supported by the cited paragraphs: Section 9 contains only mutual authority reps plus the Globix carve-out, and no indemnity/hold-harmless/defence language is present; absence of any Vendor IP indemnity is walk-away territory under INDEMN, so the finding is not over-flagging an acceptable fallback.

The inserted Section 9(c) tracks the model language on all material elements (third-party IP infringement of the Site/Services/HDI-supplied technology, HDI breach of law, HDI-caused data/Content disclosure, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with standard notice, control-of-defence (with consent limit on adverse settlements) and cooperation mechanics, and correctly declines to add any Customer indemnity.

Edit is additive only — existing p0058 text is untouched — so the change ratio reflects a genuinely required insertion rather than unnecessary rewriting; deterministic checks confirm the IP-infringement indemnity is present.

Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position and offers the standard IP exclusions as a fallback. Minor, non-disqualifying points: it relies on undefined/uncertain terms ('Services', 'Content', 'Confidential Information') and asserts survival under Section 10.7, which should be spot-checked against the actual definitions and survival clause when finalising.
